entities.name: 3,5-Difluoro-nitrobenzaldehyde
observations: Reactant structure is decoded as a difluoro nitrobenzaldehyde, approximately O=Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])c(F)cc1F.
The aldehyde carbonyl is the reactive functional group in the reported transformation.

entities.name: Difluoro-nitrobenzyl alcohol
observations: Product is the corresponding benzyl alcohol, formed by converting Ar-CHO to Ar-CH2OH while retaining nitro and aryl fluoride groups.

entities.name: Sodium borohydride
observations: Matched reaction evidence identifies NaBH4 as the likely carbonyl-reduction reagent.
The transformation is reported in tetrahydrofuran with approximately 75.2% yield over 5 hours.

entities.name: Aldehyde-to-benzyl-alcohol reduction
observations: Chemoselective reduction of an aromatic aldehyde to a primary benzyl alcohol; nitro and aryl fluoride substituents are retained.
The reaction is not consistent with oxidation, nitrosation, cyclization, or rearrangement.

entities.name: NaBH4 in THF
observations: Sodium borohydride in tetrahydrofuran is the matched condition; the database record reports about 75.2% yield over 5 hours.
Chloride appears as a spectator component in the record rather than as a key reagent.
